name: Bound keys only: the setting, its audited switch, and a preview that says what it did not decide
summary: bound_keys_only (deployment.private.json; absent/false is off) makes the wrapper refuse a line lacking a project or a principal; the switch (status/on/off, operator-gated, audited, off) previews what on would cut off, in three groups. REFUSED: the command is EXACTLY what authorized-keys prints - an absolute interpreter path (name not judged), then -E/-s alone, then this kit's wrapper (or wrapper first); no -W/-X/-i, no relay, shell-free (plain ASCII whitelist), wrapper path of at most 512 bytes, an absolute --root, unbound; group one means not served once on: would_be_refused (twenty numbers, _more, truncated). MAY BE REFUSED: every other command= line - another wrapper/root, shell syntax, a relative path, another program - printed by status and on as may_be_refused with _more, both groups printed BEFORE the write, wrapper_names_setting saying as a HINT whether the wrapper names the setting in its first 64 KiB of the OPEN descriptor (once per file; a fifo is opened non-blocking, never read); a word in a file is a hint, not a decision. on REFUSES to flip on an unreadable or partly-inspected keys file unless --without-preview is said; a NUL or over-long wrapper path costs one line.
